messages:
anna: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing staged resorption of the shared-session store into per-service stateful stores. RFC: https://go/rfcs/resorb-shared-state. TL;DR: avoid big-bang, do dual-write + read-fallback, backfill, canary cohorts. Looking for obvious gaps / tradeoffs.

sam: Sounds reasonable. Main worry is read-after-write consistency for hot routes. Dual-write + read-fallback can surface stale reads for a few seconds — ok for background jobs, not for synchronous auth checks.

liz: +1. For sync-critical paths we should keep a small proxy (read through) during migration, then retire. Also propose feature flag that flips per-tenant: `feature.resorb_shared_state = on|off`.

mike: Migration ops: plan to run bulk backfill to new stores, then tail-binlog replication for delta. If we do dual-write, we need conflict-resolve rules. Propose last-write-wins for now and log mismatches for analysis.

anna: Good call. For ordering, can we leverage request IDs in KV cache to guard against reordering? If we annotate writes with monotonic seq per-tenant, reads can pick highest seq.

sam: That helps but adds overhead. Maybe limit seq protection to top 5% busiest tenants during canary.

liz: Suggested rollout sequence:
1) infra: create per-service stores and migration roles
2) backfill + verify checksums
3) enable dual-write behind flag for cohort A
4) monitor mismatch rates & latency
5) shift read-fallback to prefer new store
6) retire proxy & turn flag on for broader cohort

mike: Ops notes: backfill command
```
./tools/backfill --src=shared_session --dst=service_sessions --batch=5000 --verify
```
Also retention: keep shared store read-only for 2 weeks after cutover.

anna: Risk register: (1) mismatch causing auth failures — mitigation: block cohort if mismatch > 0.1% for 10m. (2) increased p99 on hot routes — mitigation: limit canary size and use burst capacity.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout for tenant-cohort-A started at 1876545000 — monitoring channels: #prod-metrics #sre.

sam: Action items: sam -> implement seq guard for busy tenants; liz -> feature flag config; mike -> backfill script reviews; anna -> checklist + runbook. Let's sync Wed 11am if no major blockers.

liz: Acked. I'll draft the runbook and post link here.

anna: Thanks everyone — this should let us pay down shared-state tech debt without a risky big-bang.
